note: Recorded transcripts for the external agent runtime codecs (docs/requirements/keryx-external-agent-runtime, flow 176 T5). Every codec function is pure and is tested against these files, so the whole adapter layer runs offline on a machine with neither CLI installed. `captured: true` means the bytes came from a real run on the version named; `captured: false` means the file was hand-authored and is NOT evidence of vendor behaviour — see `caveat`.

notes: `--ephemeral` is deliberately ABSENT from baseArgv. It is mutually exclusive with resume: a thread started with it fails `resume` with `no rollout found for thread id … (code -32600)` — captured in resume-refused-ephemeral.stderr.txt. Resume is required for operator messages and for `force`, so persistence wins.

`codex exec resume` accepts a NARROWER flag set than `codex exec`: no `-s/--sandbox`, no `-C/--cd`, no `--color`. The sandbox mode is therefore not settable on resume, and the working directory must be the process cwd rather than a flag. Both constrain the runtime's resume path.
The resume handle is `thread_id`, emitted by codex on `thread.started`. keryx reads it; it cannot assign it (unlike claude's `--session-id`).

`-s` accepts `read-only | workspace-write | danger-full-access`. keryx's own vocabulary says `worktree-write`, which codex has never heard of and would reject with `error: invalid value`; the codec translates. Dormant today because only read-only is implemented, and a latent command-line failure the moment it is not.

error-word.stdout.jsonl.case: SUCCESSFUL run whose agent_message begins with `error:` — the classifier trap. A naive classifier that greps stdout for /error/ marks this a failure. Exit code is 0 and a terminal turn.completed is present.

resume.stdout.jsonl.case: resume of success.stdout.jsonl's thread; the model recalled its prior answer, proving context survives

not-logged-in.stdout.jsonl.case: no credentials (CODEX_HOME pointed at an empty directory)
not-logged-in.stdout.jsonl.notes: Top-level `error` events are a stream type the 0.1.0 spec did not model, and they arrive as RETRY NOISE — ten of them precede the single terminal `turn.failed`. A classifier must not treat the first `error` as terminal.

bad-argv.stderr.txt.case: argv rejected by this CLI version (`--no-interactive`, the flag a reference implementation shipped for months after removal)
bad-argv.stderr.txt.notes: stderr begins `error: unexpected argument …` and contains `Usage: codex exec`. Matches the `^\s*(error\b|usage:)` line filter.

usage-limit.SYNTHETIC.jsonl.caveat: HAND-AUTHORED, NOT OBSERVED. A usage limit cannot be provoked on demand. The wording is derived second-hand from a reference implementation's source comment recording a 2026-08-05 capture against an older codex, so both the phrasing and the event framing are unverified. Treat the classifier test built on this as provisional and replace the file the first time a real limit is hit.

env.why: Captured with these cleared so the fixtures reflect the subscription path the runtime actually uses.

notes: THERE ARE TWO INVOCATION SHAPES AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. `baseArgv` is one-shot: positional prompt, stdin ignored, NOT steerable. `streamingArgv` is steerable: no positional prompt, and the prompt plus every later operator message arrive on stdin as `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":…}]}}` lines. Steerability must be chosen before the process starts; there is no conversion afterwards.

`--input-format stream-json` COMBINED WITH A POSITIONAL PROMPT IS A SILENT NO-OP. Measured: the CLI ignores the prompt, waits on stdin, and with stdin closed exits 0 having written zero bytes to both streams — no error, no transcript, every process-level signal reporting success. `empty-output.stdout.jsonl` is that run's (empty) output. Specification 0.1.0 through 0.3.0 all prescribed exactly this argv.

The prompt must not sit directly behind a variadic flag (`--tools`, `--mcp-config`, `--add-dir`, `--disallowed-tools`). `--session-id`/`--resume` is the single-valued separator; a capture attempt without it failed with `MCP config file not found: …/Rep` — the CLI took the prompt's first word as a path. Note `--add-dir <directories...>` is variadic too, which the specification's prose originally omitted.
`--tools Read Grep Glob` yields a roster of exactly those three, verified in `system/init`. It is an allow-list, unlike `--allowed-tools`.
`--safe-mode` suppresses the operator's hooks and skills; without it the child emitted `system/hook_started`/`system/hook_response` and loaded ~130 slash commands.
`system/init` is multi-KB because it enumerates the tool roster and every slash command. A parser must not assume short lines.

resume.stdout.jsonl.case: resume of success.stdout.jsonl's session id; the model recalled its prior answer

not-logged-in.stdout.jsonl.case: invalid credential (bogus ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present in env)
not-logged-in.stdout.jsonl.notes: IMPORTANT — this did NOT reproduce the reference implementation's reported `Not logged in · Please run /login` on stdout with exit 0. On 2.1.220 a bogus key initialises normally, then burns eight `system/api_retry` events before terminating with `result.subtype = error_during_execution`. The practical consequence is worse than a clean refusal, not better: the failure is slow. The rule to strip `ANTHROPIC_*` stands; the evidence for it is now this file rather than the borrowed anecdote.

bad-argv.stderr.txt.notes: stderr is exactly `error: unknown option '--no-such-flag'` — terse, and notably NOT accompanied by a usage block, unlike codex.

streaming-input.stdout.jsonl.case: steerable run: `streamingArgv`, prompt delivered on stdin as `streaming-input.stdin.jsonl`
streaming-input.stdout.jsonl.notes: Proves the streaming path works and that operator messages therefore have a route. Terminates `result.subtype = success`.

streaming-input.stdin.jsonl.case: the stdin side of the run above — one JSON user message
streaming-input.stdin.jsonl.notes: Not a transcript; the input format a steerable run consumes.

empty-output.stdout.jsonl.case: the silent no-op: `--input-format stream-json` with a positional prompt and stdin closed
empty-output.stdout.jsonl.notes: ZERO BYTES, exit 0, nothing on stderr. Deliberately kept as a fixture because it is the hardest failure to detect: a classifier keyed on exit code or on stderr sees a clean success. The only signal is the absence of any terminal event. Fills the `empty output` gap earlier listed here.

usage-limit.SYNTHETIC.jsonl.caveat: HAND-AUTHORED, NOT OBSERVED. Built around the real `rate_limit_event` type seen in captured transcripts plus a terminating `result`, but the actual subtype and message a genuine limit produces are unknown. Provisional; replace on first real capture.

gaps: Both `usage-limit` fixtures are synthetic. AC6's limit case is provisional until a real quota exhaustion is captured.

No fixture exercises a multi-turn run with tool calls; every captured run is single-turn. So `tool_call`, `tool_result` and `thinking` mappings are modelled from the vendors' block schemas, not from a recording — the codecs read those defensively and omit `detail` when a field is missing.
codex has no `empty output` fixture. The claude one exists only because the silent-no-op argv produced it; no prompt tried made either CLI return an empty *successful* result.
